candidate_under_attack: Failaka rows 147.1/148.1 as clean 090/091 Gulf route/register support
tier_after_check: demoted support; source-visible Failaka pressure but object-to-row unresolved

source.publication: Steffen Terp Laursen, The westward transmission of Indus Valley sealing technology
source.local_access_attempt: Direct shell download was blocked by Cloudflare; web PDF rendering and extracted lines were usable.
relevant_lines: L1753-L1756: Failaka has only two reported examples exclusive of the Dilmun Type seal with pseudo-Indus script, Fig. 9/13.
L1758-L1764: Fig. 9/13 is a unique Dilmun seal with unparalleled Indus-like script and stands later than the Gulf Type seals.
L1765-L1770: Fig. 9/13 and also seal no.12 from Failaka may be replicas made from heavily curated/heirloom Indus-inscription models.
L1883-L1885: the two Failaka seals stand out morphologically, iconographically, and stylistically as late emulations.

confirms: There are indeed two core Failaka objects in the relevant discussion, including Kjaerum 1983 no.319 and no.279 via the existing Laursen/Kjaerum queue.
At least one Failaka object in this pair is explicitly characterized by Laursen as pseudo-Indus or unparalleled Indus-like script in a later Dilmun-style context.
does_not_confirm: The source does not map local row 147.1 to Kjaerum no.319 or no.279.

decision.effect: Do not let the two Failaka rows carry a clean Meluhha/Gulf Type phonetic bridge. They can support only a narrower Gulf/Dilmun emulation-route hypothesis until Kjaerum catalogue pages map the local rows and sign bands.

model_update: 090/091 remains a live external-contact sign class, but the most honest current version is not 'portable Meluhha marker'. It is 'Gulf/Dilmun circular-seal route or emulation marker, possibly preserving or imitating Indus sign order'.

next_decisive_tests.test: Obtain Kjaerum 1983 no.319 and no.279 catalogue pages or plate images and map them to local rows 147.1/148.1.
next_decisive_tests.promotion_condition: Both local 090-bearing rows map cleanly to the source objects and the signs are not merely pseudo-Indus decorative imitation.
next_decisive_tests.kill_condition: The Kjaerum pages map one or both local rows to different signs, or the 090-bearing row is the explicitly late pseudo-Indus no.279 without a parallel Gulf Type row.

next_decisive_tests.test: Split the external 090/091 route statistic into Gulf Type, Dilmun Type/pseudo-Indus, and classic Indus-style classes.
next_decisive_tests.promotion_condition: 090/091 remains enriched inside true Gulf Type/classic external Indus rows after excluding late pseudo-Indus emulations.
next_decisive_tests.kill_condition: The enrichment is carried mainly by late Dilmun/pseudo-Indus emulations.
